title: Assistant Constellation — breadboard notes
content:
BREADBOARD: Assistant Constellation (personal lab notes)

Quick intent: sketch a lightweight, modular orchestration that composes small 'micro-assistants' (search, code-edit, summarizer, policy-checker) into a single session-level experience. Breadboard = quick proto: wiring connectors and tradeoffs, not final API.

Why?
- Product problem: single large assistant tries to do everything; hard to scale, fine-tune, and optimize cost per micro-task.
- Hypothesis: splitting capabilities into specialized micro-assistants + a thin conductor can reduce cost, improve latency for common ops, and allow incremental rollout of experimental components.

High-level idea
- Constellation = collection of named micro-assistants (MA).
  - Each MA has: capability tag(s), model/variant pointer, cost profile, latency SLO, input/response contract (schema).
- Conductor = lightweight orchestrator that: intent-classifies request, routes sub-tasks to MAs, merges responses, enforces fallback policies, tracks cost/latency per MA.
- Session Halo = small session-level context manager that maintains affinities (which MA served well for a user/activity) and sticky routing.

User personas / primary scenarios
1) Developer assistant: user asks to refactor a function + run tests.
   - Orchestration: code-edit MA -> test-run microservice (sidecar), QA summarizer MA.
2) Sales enablement: summarize recent calls and extract action items.
   - Orchestration: transcription MA -> summarizer MA -> entity-extractor MA.
3) Support bot: triage a ticket and produce patch suggestion.
   - Orchestration: triage classifier -> knowledge-base retriever MA -> patch-gen MA -> policy-check MA.

Concrete benefits (measurable)
- Cost per composite task down by X% if heavy generative spans are limited to specific MAs. (measure: cost-per-task pre/post)
- Latency: parallelize independent subcalls -> p75 latency improve.
- Reliability: use lightweight fallback (cached summary) instead of full gen when MA unavailable.
- Experimentation: swap a single MA with newer quantized model without touching others.

API / contract sketch (thought experiment)
- POST /v1/constellations/run
  - body: { session_id, intent_hint, steps: [ {role: "summarize", hints: {...}}, {role: "extract", schema: ...} ], budget_ms, cost_limit }
  - response: { orchestrator_log, steps: [{ma: "summarizer-v2", status: "ok", out: {...}}], final: {merged_output} }
- Lightweight SDK: client can declare 'soft-constraints' (max-cost, prefer-low-latency) and conductor adapts routing.

Session affinity heuristics (Session Halo)
- Maintain small per-session affinity map: { capability -> preferred_MA, last_success_ts, failure_count } (TTL ~ 24h).
- Use: reduce routing churn, warm KV caches for MA, bias toward cheaper MA when similar quality.

Routing policy primitives (to support product knobs)
- prefer_latency / prefer_cost / prefer_quality (weights)
- canary_percentage for new MA
- fallback_chain: list of compatible MA by cost/quality
- regional_only (for data residency)

Data, privacy & compliance notes
- MAs may have different data residency/PII policies: conductor must annotate and prevent cross-region mixing.
- Audit log per subcall mandatory (who/which MA, model version, input hash).

Experiments to run (MVP -> v1)
MVP (breadboard):
- Provide 3 MAs: summarizer (small opt), retriever (dense+bm25), generator (baseline Llama-like).
- Conductor implementing: intent-classify (cheap), sequential routing for dependent steps, parallel for independent ones, simple merge rule: prefer generator outputs unless flagged low-confidence.
- Metrics to capture: p50/p95 latency, cost-per-composite, success rate (human eval for N tasks), error surface by MA.

A/B experiments
- A: monolith assistant (baseline) vs. constellation conductor routing identical tasks. Measure cost + user satisfaction.
- B: affinity learning on/off: does sticky routing reduce user friction/latency?

Integration with Redwood features (ops)
- Dedicated: pin mission-critical MAs to dedicated pools for latency guarantees.
- Private: offer per-customer MA catalog (customer-provided models).
- Console: surface MA-level dashboards (tokens, latency, failures) and per-constellation rollout controls (canary, rollback).

Edge cases & failure modes
- Partial success: some MAs fail -> conductor must synthesize graceful degraded reply (e.g., "I couldn't fetch the test run, here's a patch suggestion based on the diff").
- Schema mismatch: MA returns unexpected shape -> reject & fallback.
- Cost runaway: many parallel MAs -> conductor must enforce cost_limit and short-circuit lower-utility steps.

Open questions / unknowns
- How granular should MA contracts be? (full JSON schema vs. simple text blob+metadata)
- Cost accounting per substep: attribute to customer + feature? multi-tenant complexity.
- Intent classifier accuracy requirements to avoid misrouting (false positives causing heavy gen).
- How to do human eval at scale for composite multi-MA outputs?

Prototype timeline (very rough)
- Week 0-2: breadboard conductor + 3 toy MAs; simple SDK; local eval harness.
- Week 3-6: integrate retriever+summarizer, run small A/B, collect cost/latency signals.
- Month 2: add affinity/localization, add console dashboard prototype.

Notes to self (todo / quick tasks)
- Draft minimal JSON contract for MA responses (fields: text, confidence, tokens_used, meta).
- Wire small harness that can run a "recipe" (steps array) and log subcall traces.
- Talk to Jordan Kim about retrieval/caching tradeoffs (JIRA-7890).
- Quick user interviews: 6 devs who use assistant heavily — what micro-capabilities do they wish were isolated?

Cheap wins to try now
- Implement sticky routing for summarizer for users who request meeting notes repeatedly.
- Add cost_limit param and enforce cheapest fallback for non-critical steps.

Longer-term thoughts
- Marketplace of MAs (third-party models) with vetting & billing share.
- Auto-synthesis of orchestrations: given a few examples, system suggests step decomposition.
- Learning-based conductor: use past session success to route adaptively (bandit/rl approach).

Final: this doc is a messy breadboard. Keep it small and hackable. Next step: convert to 1-page PRD for exec + separate technical spike ticket list.

-- mika
